Short answer: pick a modern LED task lamp with dimming and adjustable color temperature (2700–6500 K), high efficacy (≥80 lm/W), and an Energy Star or DLC listing. From your saved catalog I found one candidate named "Meadowlight Lamp" — I can check its specs if you want, but the catalog entry in memory has no provenance/details, so its claims need verification.

Why that class of lamp
- LEDs are far more efficient than incandescent/halogen: typical LED task lamps use about 5–15 W to deliver the same useful light as a 40–60 W incandescent. That’s lower energy use and lower heat output. (Evidence: widely established LED performance — still verify the exact lumen-per-watt for any model.)
- Dimming saves energy and extends lifetime when full brightness isn’t required.
- Adjustable color temperature improves comfort and task performance (cooler light for detail, warmer for general comfort).
- High CRI (>90) is important if accurate color rendering is needed (design, photo work).
- Energy Star / DLC listings are a quick way to confirm independently tested energy performance.

What I found in your catalog
- Meadowlight Lamp — appears in the catalog search results. I could not find provenance or detailed specs in memory (no extractor/source info returned). That means:
  - Claims about its wattage, lumens, CRI, dimming, color temp range, and certifications in the catalog should be verified against the product page or spec sheet.
  - Verify warranty, expected lifetime (hours), and any smart features (sensors, app control) before purchasing.

Practical selection checklist (use this to compare models)
- Wattage and lumens: target ~400–1,000 lm output for desk task lighting; lower wattage with higher efficacy is better (look for lumens per watt).
- Efficacy: ≥80 lm/W preferred (higher is better).
- CRI: ≥80 acceptable; ≥90 recommended for color-accurate work.
- Color temperature: adjustable 2700–6500 K or at least two presets (warm/cool).
- Dimmable: smooth, flicker-free dimming (look for PWM frequency or driver info if specified).
- Certifications: Energy Star or DesignLights Consortium (DLC) listed recommended.
- Controls: tactile dimmer, memory for last setting, or smart scheduling/occupancy sensor for additional savings.
- Physical range: articulating arm and head with good range of motion and glare control.
- Lifetime/warranty: rated lifetime (e.g., 30,000–50,000 hours) and at least 1–2 year warranty.

Quick energy-savings example (to compare)
- Example LED: 10 W, used 8 hours/day -> 0.01 kW × 8 = 0.08 kWh/day → ~2.4 kWh/month.
- Example incandescent: 40 W, used 8 hours/day -> 0.04 kW × 8 = 0.32 kWh/day → ~9.6 kWh/month.
- At $0.15/kWh, monthly cost LED ≈ $0.36 vs incandescent ≈ $1.44. Savings per lamp are modest but scale across an office.

- Look up full specs for the Meadowlight Lamp in the catalog (wattage, lumens, CRI, color temp, certifications) and verify claims against product pages — I have the catalog hit but need permission to fetch or you can paste the product details.
- If you want model suggestions beyond your catalog, tell me style/budget/feature priorities (e.g., USB charging, smart control, very high CRI) and I’ll recommend specific models and cite sources.
